JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that took place on 28.04.2023.
2.
The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:

On 28.04.2023 at about 1.30 p.m., after finishing his work, when the petitioner was climbing the KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-13-F-2461 on SRS Junction NH.4,
Tumkuru-Bangalore Road, Peenya at Bangalore City, at that time the driver of the said bus suddenly moved the bus without any indication or signal in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
It is contended that, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Ravi Kirloskar Memorial hospital, wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment,
medicine etc.,
3.
It is contended that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as Home Guard and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as he was doing earlier and lost his income.
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-13-F-2461.
Hence, the respondent being the owner/insurer of the offending bus is liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent has appeared through its learned counsel and filed objection statement.
5. The Respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

It has denied the age, occupation and Ashok Kumar.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123638191/
2 income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.

It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
On other grounds prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner prove that on 28.04.2023 at about 1.30 p.m., when he was climbing the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-13-F-2461, on SRS Junction, NH-04, Tumkuru- Bengaluru road, Peenya, Bengaluru City, at that time the driver of the said bus suddenly moved it without the signal in a rash and negligent manner, due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or Award?

On the other hand, respondent has examined one witness as RW.1.
8. Heard the arguments.

Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...
As per final order For the following:

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending bus driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation Ashok Kumar.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123638191/

sentences.text: Contending the above facts, the petitioners prayed to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, police intimation, notice and its reply, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

On the other hand, respondent has examined its driver as RW.1.
12.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC Bus.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened on SRS Junction NH-4,
Tumkuru-Bangalore Road, Peenya at Bangalore City, at that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-13-F-2461 suddenly moved it without the signal in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.

The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazer and Sketch prepared at the time of spot Ashok Kumar.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123638191/
4 mahazer.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 it reflects KSRTC bus has given stop in that junction for climbing the passenger, that time injured was climbing the KSRTC bus from front door at that time the driver of the bus without observing this suddenly moved the bus, due to that petitioner fell down and got injured.
If the driver of KSRTC Bus drove it normal speed by observing the passengers who were climbing the bus at that junction, then he slowly moved his bus, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.8 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P10 was also filed as against the driver of the KSRTC Bus.

14. It has to be noted that, in the instant case, the Respondent who is insurer of the KSRTC Bus has disputed the occurrence of this accident involving the insured KSRTC Bus bearing No.
KA-13-F-2461.

The said insurer has taken contention that, when the KSRTC bus reached SRS Juction NH-4, Tumkur, Bengaluru during that time petitioner entered the bus in front door during that time his luggage bag wase stopping from his body he got down from the bus, then the said KSRTC driver slowly moved the bus, the person touched to his right side leg to front left side wheel of the said bus suffered minor injuries and the said SRS Junction is not a bus stop the said accident was occurred purely on the part of the petitioner.

In support of their version respondent has examined the driver of the bus namely Ravi H.G., as Rw.1.
15.

Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing is elicited from his mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P5 coupled with Ex.P7.
These documents clearly demonstrated that there is negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving by the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-13-F-2461 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-13-F-2461.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

Petitioner in order to prove his disability, examined one witness as PW.2 and he got marked Ex.P16 to P18.
17.
LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was Home Guard and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and to prove the same,
petitioner has not produced any documents.

In the absence of document of income,
the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2023.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- per month.

5
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.
In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained crush injury right foot-open fracture, dislocation distal phalanx of great toe.
He was treated conservatively.
On clinical examination conducted by him he found that the petitioner has lost great toe.
He has assessed permanent physical disability to the right lower limb at 10%.

Further, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajaykumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows;
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to Ashok Kumar.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123638191/
6 earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.
By applying the said precedent to the present case the petitioner is facing difficulty in doing day today activities.
Petitioner has also sustained other injuries.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 05%.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 36 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 28.04.2023.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P12 Aadhar card as 01.09.1986, the petitioner was aged 37 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 37 is 15 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,44,000/-(Rs.16,000x12x15x5/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

18. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
Wound certificate produced at Ex.P9, the discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
The Ex.P9 wound certificate Ravi Kirloskar Memorial Hospital reveals that petitioner took treatment on 28.04.2023 as out patient.

Thereafter as per Ex.P11 Discharge Summary of Ravi Kirloskar Memorial Hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 28.04.2023 to 01.05.2023 and took conservative treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.40,000/- towards pain and sufferings.

7 19.
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.75,069/- as per Ex.P13 and prescriptions at Ex.P14.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.75,069/- and he is entitled for the same.

20. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 4 days, and also took follow treatment as out patient. Certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.4,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least one month.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.16,000/- (16,000 X 1) under this head.

22. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 37 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 05% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.20,000/- on this head.
23. FUTURE MEDICAL AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor has not suggested anything about the future surgery to be undergone by the petitioner, hence petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this head.

24. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:

25.
The petitioner is claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
26. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-F-2461.
In the present case, respondent No.1 is the Managing Director, KSRTC is the statutory owner of the offending bus involved in the accident.
Respondent No.2 is the Divisional Manager, Hassan Division has been impleaded only in his official capacity to represent the concerned division of KSRTC.
Since the driver of the KSRTC bus was negligent in causing the accident, the KSRTC, being the employer and owner of the bus, is vicariously liable to compensate the claimant.
Respondent No.2, being only an administrative officer of the Hassan Division, is not personally liable.
Accordingly, the liability to pay compensation is fixed on respondent No.1 - KSRTC, represented by its Managing Director.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
Further, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajaykumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows;
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.
Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P12 Aadhar card as 01.09.1986, the petitioner was aged 37 years at the time of accident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,44,000/-(Rs.16,000x12x15x5/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.
Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.
In the present case, respondent No.1 is the Managing Director, KSRTC is the statutory owner of the offending bus involved in the accident.
Since the driver of the KSRTC bus was negligent in causing the accident, the KSRTC, being the employer and owner of the bus, is vicariously liable to compensate the claimant.
Respondent No.2, being only an administrative officer of the Hassan Division, is not personally liable.
